description: Sync Zendesk Support tickets and their comments from the brands you choose. Group-based ticket access carries over when Enforce ACL is on and HydraDB can work out the readers.
opening: Sync Zendesk Support tickets from the brands you select, with every comment on them: public replies and internal notes. Each ticket is one document and each comment is its own document, linked to its ticket. PDF and DOCX files attached to comments are read, and their text is searchable with the comment.

A ticket assigned to a group can be restricted to that group's members, the assignee, the requester and Zendesk admins. A ticket with no assigned group carries no Zendesk permissions. Search applies these restrictions only when Enforce ACL is on. Authorize as a Zendesk administrator, or only that person's own tickets sync. Satisfaction ratings and Help Center articles are not synced.

permissions.who_can_read: A ticket with an assigned group can be read by the group's members, the assignee, the requester and Zendesk admins. A comment can be read by its ticket's readers. The requester cannot read an internal note, unless they also have access as an admin, the assignee or a group member.
permissions.when_unreadable: If a group's memberships are missing or incomplete, a member cannot be identified, a ticket has too many readers, or a comment's ticket cannot be found, the item gets a permission warning, which you can find with `additional_metadata.rbac_warning`.
notes: A ticket with no assigned group carries no Zendesk permissions and gets no warning. It follows the access rule you set on its resource. With no rule, it is visible to everyone who can query the collection, and so are its comments, including internal notes.
Readers come from the assigned group and the people named on the ticket. Other Zendesk visibility settings are not reproduced.
Readers are worked out when a ticket is synced. Do not rely on a change to Zendesk group membership to remove access right away.

connect.auth: Zendesk uses an OAuth access token, with a refresh token and the OAuth client id and secret so HydraDB can renew it. OAuth is the recommended option for a new connection. An existing Zendesk API token also works.

credentials.name: subdomain
credentials.text: Your Zendesk subdomain, for example `acme` for `acme.zendesk.com`.

credentials.name: refresh_token
credentials.text: The OAuth refresh token, used to renew the access token.

credentials.name: api_token
credentials.text: A Zendesk API token. Send it with `subdomain` and `email`.

credentials.name: email
credentials.text: The email of the Zendesk user the API token belongs to.

permissions.name: Administrator
permissions.text: the Zendesk role of the person who authorizes. Otherwise only that person's own tickets sync.

steps.title: Authorize as an administrator
steps.text: Sign in to Zendesk as an administrator and authorize the connection with the `read` scope.

steps.title: Create the connector
steps.text: Enter `subdomain` and the OAuth token fields.

steps.title: Select brands
steps.text: HydraDB lists the account's brands. Select the ones to sync. Tickets from every brand are still read from Zendesk and filtered afterwards. A comment follows its ticket's brand.

connect.account: One connector reads one Zendesk subdomain.

sync.first_sync: Each selected brand reaches back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default. Comments come with the tickets in that window.
sync.changes: Each sync reads tickets changed since the last sync, with their comments.
sync.edits: A changed ticket is read again with its comments and updates their documents.
sync.deletes: Tickets deleted in Zendesk can stay searchable in HydraDB.
notes: Zendesk users, groups, group memberships and organizations are read for the whole account on every sync, whatever brands you select. They name people and decide who can read a ticket. They are not documents of their own.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.zendesk_id
shared_attributes.text: The ticket id on a ticket, the comment id on a comment. Targets one item, and keeps later syncs on the same document. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.rbac_warning
shared_attributes.text: Set when HydraDB could not fully work out who can read the item, or when a group that granted access was deleted. A warning does not by itself mean the item is public. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: connector_id
shared_attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's items. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: acl
shared_attributes.text: The people who can read the item, worked out as described under Permissions. Not searchable.

documents.name: Tickets
documents.title: The ticket subject. A ticket without one gets a title with its ticket id.
documents.text: The ticket description, or the subject when the description is empty. Then `Requester`, `Assignee`, `Organization` and `Group` lines. The status, priority and creation time are part of the text too. The subject is searchable too.
documents.date: When the ticket was last updated, else when it was created.
documents.link_back: The ticket in the Zendesk agent interface.
documents.files: None on the ticket itself. Attachments are on its comments.

attributes.name: status
attributes.text: New, open, pending, hold, solved or closed, written as a `Status` line.

attributes.name: priority
attributes.text: Urgent, high, normal or low, written as a `Priority` line.

attributes.name: requester
attributes.text: The requester's name, written as the `Requester` line, where HydraDB can identify the customer.

attributes.name: assignee
attributes.text: The assigned agent's name, written as the `Assignee` line. The graph records the ticket as assigned to that agent.

attributes.name: organization
attributes.text: The organization's name, written as the `Organization` line, where HydraDB can identify the company.

attributes.name: group
attributes.text: The assigned group's name, written as the `Group` line. Who can read the ticket is worked out from the group's members, not from this name.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the ticket was created, written as a `Created` line. Used as the result date only when the update time is missing.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the ticket was last updated. Not searchable.

attributes.name: tags
attributes.text: The ticket's tags. They are not part of the searchable text.

attributes.name: api_url
attributes.text: The ticket's address in the Zendesk API. The link back is the agent interface address.

documents.name: Comments
documents.one_document: One comment on a ticket: a public reply or an internal note.
documents.title: `Comment by` and the author's name. Without an author, the first 80 characters of the comment.
documents.text: An `Author` line, then the plain text of the comment, or `Attachment:` and the file name for a comment that has only an attachment. The ticket id and the creation time are part of the text too.
documents.link_back: None. Open the ticket from its own document.
documents.files: PDF and DOCX attachments up to 25 MiB are downloaded and read, and their text is searchable with the comment. An attachment that fails HydraDB's checks is skipped. Documents in other formats are not read.

attributes.name: author
attributes.text: The name of the person who wrote the comment, written as the `Author` line. The graph records the comment as written by that person.

attributes.name: mentions
attributes.text: Names @mentioned in an internal note. The names stay in the note text, and the graph records each as mentioned.

attributes.name: parent_id
attributes.text: The ticket the comment belongs to, written into the text as the ticket id. Links the comment to its ticket. The ticket's text is read together with the comment.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.zendesk_ticket_id
attributes.text: The id of the ticket the comment belongs to. Returns every comment on one ticket. Not searchable.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the comment was created, written as a `Created` line.

attributes.name: public
attributes.text: True for a public reply, false for an internal note. The requester cannot read an internal note through being the requester. Not searchable.

attributes.name: author_id
attributes.text: The Zendesk user id of the comment's author.

example_searches: What did we tell Acme about the export bug?
Which urgent tickets are open for the billing group?
What did an agent write on ticket 123?

people: The assigned agent of each ticket.
The requester, the organization and the group appear in the ticket text, where HydraDB can identify them.
graph.from_text: The ticket description with its requester, assignee, organization and group lines, the comment text, and the text of attached PDF and DOCX files. Each comment is read together with its ticket's text.

not_synced: Help Center articles and community posts.
Ticket audits, macros, ticket fields and forms, SLA policies and metric events.
Attached documents in formats other than PDF and DOCX.
